## Conclusions
- **WiSE-FT does not help here.** Moving the fine-tuned weights back toward the pretrained ones costs accuracy
  on RefCOCOg-LPCVC at every blend: -1.6 (a=0.75), -5.5 (0.5), -10.9 (0.25). On the LPCVC sample all blends are
  within ±0.8 of the fully fine-tuned model (noise). So the fine-tune is not over-specialized in a way blending
  can fix, and **we keep a = 1 (fully fine-tuned).** We did not tune a on validation; every blend is worse or equal.
- **First significant gain on real LPCVC data:** fine-tuned B (010) vs. pretrained B on the 56-image LPCVC
  sample is **+2.16 [+0.4, +4.2]** (paired bootstrap; FP32). The unpaired CIs overlap, but the paired test resolves it.
- **FP32 re-evaluation of the trained checkpoints** (all numbers in this table are FP32 PyTorch; training-time
  numbers were bf16): 010 = 87.28, 012 (distill) = 81.86, 013 (cross-source) = 84.30. These differ from the bf16
  training logs by ≤ 0.1, and the conclusions of 012 and 013 are unchanged (both significantly below 010 on RefCOCOg-LPCVC,
  both equal to it on the sample).
- **Decision:** submission candidate = `mobileclip2-b#checkpoints/010_ft-b-contrastive/model.pt` (17.68 ms on the S22, exp 011).
